blocks.text: Professional sump pump installation in Terrell Hills, TX, will ensure that your pump works correctly even during heavy rainstorms.
The installation of this equipment must take into consideration several important details, such as choosing the right pump, placing it properly, and confirming that the discharge line is flowing.
If something malfunctions with your pump, professional sump pump repair from Rosenberg Plumbing & Air is ideal. We can get your pump working again before you experience extensive water damage.

Selecting the correct sump pump for your home’s size and needs is important. For example, living in an area with very damp soil may warrant a larger and more capable pump to ensure your home stays dry.

If your pump is in an area where a lot of people pass by or it’s near bedrooms, you may want to consider investing in a pump that operates quietly. For minimal maintenance and repairs, talk to our team about a submersible pump.

The placement of your sump pump is very important. It should be in your basement, but at the lowest point in that area. This allows for the proper collection of water. Various parts will contribute to the overall function of your pump, including a check valve, which prevents water from flowing back into the pit.

A discharge pipe moves water away from your sump pit and your home. A sump pump runs off electricity, so there will be electrical connections that are near an area with a lot of water. Our team will make sure that your pump plugs into a GFCI outlet for safety purposes.
A lot of homeowners choose to install a battery backup on their pump. If the power goes out at your residence, the battery will keep your pump running and engage automatically.

It’s normal for a sump pump to experience wear and tear over time. Its average life expectancy is approximately 7 to 10 years. Different components can wear out, including the float switch, pump, motor, or impeller.
Our plumbers will inspect and diagnose a problem quickly so a repair can occur before your basement floods. Moisture can quickly lead to mold growth, wood rot or other issues.
